newsitem.title: CANADA: Cambridge sees cash flow rise after merger.
newsitem.headline: Cambridge sees cash flow rise after merger.

text.p: Cambridge Shopping Centres Ltd on Monday said its cash flow should increase by about 10 percent per share on an annual basis following its friendly takeover of Markborough Properties Inc.
The company also told a news conference that it will assume about C$1.0 billion of Markborough's debt as part of the merger.

"We expect the transaction to be accretive to our shareholders. We think that should be in the 10 percent plus range when the dust has all settled and we've sorted out exactly where we're going to be on combined overhead expenses," said Donald Priddle, chief financial officer of Cambridge Shopping Centres.
Priddle said the company's assets will grow to about C$3.5 billion from C$2.2 billion before the merger.

Cambridge shares were up C$0.45 to C$10.15 in early afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange following the announcement. Markborough shares fell C$0.08 to C$0.46, which is the price per share of the Cambridge offer.
